q: Create a constant `addButton`: the button named 'Add to cart'.
a: const addButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' });
note: No await: a locator is only a description.

Locator: the level 1 heading named 'Products'.
Locator: the link whose name STARTS WITH 'Cart' (regex /^Cart/), whatever number follows.
Locator: the checkbox named 'I agree to the terms'.
a: page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'I agree to the terms' })

Locator: the input with the placeholder 'What needs to be done?'.
Locator: elements whose WHOLE text is exactly 'QA'.
Locator: the text matching 'hello, sam' ignoring case (regex).
Locator: the element with data-testid="cart-count".
Locator (CSS, last resort): elements with the class 'price'.
Create `rows`: the rows INSIDE the table named 'Employees'.

q: Error: strict mode violation: getByRole('button', { name: 'Edit' }) resolved to 5 elements. What does it mean and how do you fix it?
a: An action needs exactly one element, but the locator matches 5. Make it precise: chain/filter (e.g. the row with 'Eva Rocha', then its Edit button). Use first()/nth() only if position is what you mean.

q: Locator priority, from best to last resort?
a: getByRole > getByLabel > getByPlaceholder > getByText > getByAltText/getByTitle > getByTestId > locator('css')

q: How does { name: 'Open' } match by default?
a: Substring and case-insensitive: 'Open alert', 'open confirm'... all match. Use exact: true or a regex to be strict.

q: Why does getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Password' }) find nothing?
a: <input type="password"> has no ARIA role. Use getByLabel('Password').

q: Does `const btn = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add' });` need await? Why?
a: No. Creating a locator only describes the element; Playwright searches when you use it (click, expect, count...).

q: Two ways to find the role and accessible name of an element?
a: 1) 'Pick locator' in codegen / UI mode / Inspector. 2) DevTools (F12) -> Elements -> Accessibility tab (Role + Name).
